1.name: Body
1.note: The block with the two overlapping bores. The gear tips run close to the bore wall, which seals each tooth space as a batch.

2.name: Front flange
2.note: Closes the shaft end of the body, carries the shaft seal and locates the pump on the motor or engine.

3.name: Rear cover
3.note: Closes the back of the body.

4.name: Drive gear shaft
4.note: The input. It turns the driven gear and carries oil round the bore in its tooth spaces.

5.name: Driven gear shaft
5.note: Turned by the drive gear. Where the two gears mesh, the teeth squeeze the oil out to the outlet.

6.name: Front bushing
6.note: Bronze pieces on the flange side. They hold the gear faces to keep the end leak small, and carry the shafts.

7.name: Rear bushing
7.note: The same on the cover side. Pressure behind them presses them against the gears, which closes the gap.

8.name: Plain bearing
8.note: Journal bearings for the shaft ends.

9.name: Shaft seal
9.note: Lip seal on the drive shaft that keeps oil from leaking out of the flange.

10.name: Circlip
10.note: Holds the shaft seal in the flange.

11.name: Parallel key
11.note: Transmits the input torque from the coupling to the drive shaft.

12.name: Screw
12.note: Clamps the flange, body and cover together against the oil pressure.

14.name: Body seal
14.note: Figure-8 seals between the body and each end plate, keeping oil in at both joints.

15.name: Balance seal
15.note: Defines the pressurised area behind the bushings, so they press on the gears just enough to close the gap.
